traditional: Sun square the Moon: a hard contact. The body, home, and daily needs works against vitality, authority, and recognition - obstruction, friction, and strained outcomes in these areas.
modern: Identity and emotion, the outer self and the inner life. How who you present yourself to be lines up (or doesn't) with what you actually feel and need. Psychologically the square is inner tension to integrate: Ego needs and emotional needs pull from conflicting sources, so the public self and the private self work at cross purposes and have to be reconciled. The growth is owning both sides instead of splitting them.

cyclic.waxing: Crisis of action: take conscious hold and build a durable form for feeling against selfhood, or be thrown off course.
cyclic.waning: Crisis of meaning: break down the feeling/selfhood form that has outlived its purpose and reorient toward the next cycle.

business: Friction in this area. Self-direction reads as either steady and integrated, or as internal conflict that undercuts decisiveness.
shadow: Moodiness and over-need collides with egotism and needing to be the center; forcing or splitting it instead of working it through.
arcApplying: Friction builds toward a forced adjustment.
arcSeparating: The crisis passes; what was restructured settles.

readerCopy.summary: The plan may still look good on paper while your actual life is starting to reject it.
readerCopy.body: The plan may still look good on paper while your actual life is starting to reject it. When the Sun squares the Moon, what you are trying to accomplish rubs against what your body, home, emotions, or existing responsibilities need from you. Exhaustion, irritability, or the sudden urge to cancel everything may be less about the goal itself and more about what the current version is demanding. Change the schedule, expectation, or responsibility that is making the rest of the plan unnecessarily hard to carry.
